Hi! My name is Yunus Maranki.

For my bachelor's thesis at the University of Bonn I have
formalized o-minimality in lean. I formalized the monotonicity theorem for o-minimal structures and also the extreme value theorem for definably complete structures.

There is a previous formalization of o-minimality from 2020 by Reid Barton and Johan Commelin. I defined o-minimality similar to how they defined it, but instead of definability without logic I used the model-theoretic
definability that mathlib today has.

I also added an aesop tactic for solving easy definability goals (such automation has been discussed here).

I did not prove o-minimality for any structure. But maybe if quantifier elimination gets added to mathlib, o-minimality of real closed fields could be formalized.

Would any of these results be a good fit for mathlib? The code currently does not have mathlib quality and I am not sure if there is a better way to design the definability tactic. But I could try to improve the code and then open small PRs.

IMO o-minimality would probably be a great fit for mathlib, I don't know much about o-minimality but on one of my recent research livestreams I realized that it's connected to things like tactics for deciding asymptotic relationships between common functions (c.f. #General announcements > New tactic: `compute_asymptotics` ) so it feels like it could be of big practical importance, in addition to being the research topic of a recent Fields medal winner.
